candidates.name: OS Net positioning data
verified_facts: OS Net is a national GNSS base-station network supporting real-time and post-processed correction data with centimetre-level positioning under suitable workflows.
The service uses around 120 base stations and provides access to the national coordinate reference system.
semantic_limits: Network capability or centimetre-level service positioning does not equal a parcel ground-height observation; local GNSS hardware, environment, processing, antenna, transformation and terrain-source errors remain separate.

candidates.name: Antenna phase centre offsets
verified_facts: OS states that differences in antenna phase-centre offsets must be included in GNSS data processing, especially for height accuracy.

The RINEX antenna height is measured to the antenna reference point and phase-centre offsets are then applied; elevation-dependent phase-centre variation should be modelled for highest geodetic accuracy.
semantic_limits: Ignoring antenna phase-centre modelling can bias GNSS height, so OS Net/control accuracy cannot be used as the complete parcel-height error budget.
